categories.title: Tax Benefit Components
categories.blurb: Salary components that legally reduce your tax bill.

hra.title: House Rent Allowance (HRA)
hra.short: Tax-free part of your salary when you pay rent.
hra.whatIsIt: HRA is a part of your salary that your employer pays you to help with rent. A portion of it can be tax-free (exempt) if you actually pay rent for a house you live in. The exempt portion is not added to your taxable income, so you pay less tax.
hra.benefit: Instead of paying tax on the whole HRA, you pay tax only on the part that is not exempt. For someone in the 30% slab, every ₹1,00,000 of HRA that becomes exempt saves roughly ₹31,200 in tax (including 4% cess).
whoCanClaim: Salaried employees who receive HRA as part of their salary.
You must actually pay rent and live in the rented house.
You must be under the OLD tax regime. HRA exemption is not available in the new regime.

howCalculated.intro: The exempt amount is the LOWEST of these three. Everything else is taxable.
steps: The actual HRA your employer pays you.
Rent you pay minus 10% of your Basic + DA (dearness allowance).
50% of Basic + DA if you live in one of the specified metro cities, otherwise 40% of Basic + DA.

clauses.title: Old regime only
clauses.text: You can claim HRA exemption only if you choose the old tax regime. Under the new regime this deduction is not available.

clauses.title: Rent must be actually paid
clauses.text: You need proof of rent paid, such as rent receipts, a rental agreement or bank transfer records. Your employer may ask for these.

clauses.title: Landlord PAN above ₹1 lakh
clauses.text: If the rent you pay is more than ₹1,00,000 in a year (about ₹8,333 a month), you must give your landlord's PAN to your employer.

clauses.title: Rent to parents is allowed
clauses.text: You can pay rent to your parents and claim HRA, as long as the rent is real, paid by bank transfer, and your parents show it as income in their return.

clauses.title: No HRA in salary? Use 80GG
clauses.text: If your salary has no HRA component, you may still claim a deduction for rent under Section 80GG (old regime), capped at ₹5,000 per month, subject to conditions such as not owning a house in the same city.

clauses.title: Who is on the law's list
clauses.text: In the old Act this was Section 10(13A) with Rule 2A. The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaced the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026, and the rules carry over. Published sources disagree on the exact new section number, so it is not stated here until confirmed from the official text.

latestUpdate.headline: 50% HRA limit now covers 8 metro cities (up from 4).
details: Before 1 April 2026, only Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai had the higher 50% limit.
From 1 April 2026, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad are added. The 50% limit now applies to 8 cities.
All other cities, including Gurgaon and Noida, stay at 40%.
The change applies to tax year 2026-27. Returns for FY 2025-26 still use the old list of four cities.
Some reports say a landlord-tenant disclosure requirement was proposed in draft rules. This is not confirmed as final.

example.scenario: Meera lives in Bengaluru. Basic + DA is ₹50,000 a month. Her employer pays HRA of ₹25,000 a month. She pays rent of ₹28,000 a month.

rows.label: C. 50% of Basic+DA (new rule, Bengaluru is now a 50% city)

example.result: Exempt HRA = lowest of A, B, C = ₹23,000 a month (₹2,76,000 a year).
example.compare: Under the old 40% rule, C would have been ₹20,000, so only ₹20,000 a month would be exempt. The change gives Meera ₹36,000 more exempt income a year, which saves about ₹11,200 in tax at the 30% slab.

documents: Rent receipts or rental agreement
Bank transfer proof of rent
Landlord's name, address and PAN (if rent above ₹1 lakh a year)
Declaration submitted to your employer's payroll
watchOut: Pick the old regime in your declaration, or your employer will not give you the exemption.
Pay rent by bank transfer, not cash, so you can prove it.
The city is decided by where you live, not where your office is.
If you skipped claiming it at work, you can still claim it when you file your return.

cea.title: Children Education Allowance (CEA)
cea.short: Tax-free part of your salary for your children's schooling.
cea.whatIsIt: CEA is a salary component your employer pays you towards your children's schooling. A fixed part of it is tax-free (exempt). Anything above the limit is taxed like normal salary.
cea.benefit: The exempt part is not added to your taxable income, so you pay less tax. The old limits were tiny, so most people ignored this allowance. The new limits make it worth having in your salary structure. For someone in the 30% slab, every ₹1,00,000 of CEA that becomes exempt saves roughly ₹31,200 in tax (including 4% cess).
whoCanClaim: Salaried employees whose employer pays CEA as a separate salary component.
Up to 2 children. The limit is per child, so a third child gets nothing extra.
You must be under the OLD tax regime. The exemption is not available in the new regime.
No fee receipts are needed. It is a fixed exempt amount, not a refund of actual school fees.

howCalculated.intro: Work this out for each child (maximum 2), then add the two together.
steps: Take the CEA your employer actually pays for that child.
Take the monthly limit: ₹3,000 per child for education, or ₹9,000 per child if the child lives in a hostel.
The exempt amount is the LOWER of the two. Everything above it is taxable.

clauses.title: Old regime only
clauses.text: You can claim the CEA exemption only if you choose the old tax regime.

clauses.title: Maximum 2 children
clauses.text: The exemption covers only 2 children. A third child gets no exemption.

clauses.title: Education and hostel are separate
clauses.text: Education allowance is for schooling. Hostel allowance applies only if the child lives in a hostel. Each has its own limit.

clauses.title: Fixed limit, no bills
clauses.text: You get the exemption up to the limit even if your real school fees are higher or lower. You do not need to show fee receipts.

clauses.title: Not the same as 80C tuition fees
clauses.text: Tuition fees you pay can also be claimed under Section 80C in the old regime. That is a separate deduction, and you can use both.

clauses.title: Not the same as central government CEA
clauses.text: Central government employees get a CEA under pay rules, with different amounts. That is not this income-tax exemption.

clauses.title: Where it sits in the law
clauses.text: In the old Act this was Section 10(14) with Rule 2BB. The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaced the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026. The exact new section number is not stated here until confirmed from the official text.

latestUpdate.headline: Tax-free limit raised from ₹100 to ₹3,000 per child per month.
details: Education allowance: from ₹100 to ₹3,000 per child per month.
Hostel allowance: from ₹300 to ₹9,000 per child per month.
Still limited to 2 children.
Applies from tax year 2026-27 (1 April 2026).

example.scenario: Your employer pays CEA of ₹4,000 a month for your two children (₹2,000 each).

rows.label: New limit: each child's ₹2,000 is below ₹3,000

example.result: New rule: ₹4,000 a month, or ₹48,000 a year, is exempt.
example.compare: Under the old limit only ₹2,400 a year was exempt. At the 30% slab the new rule saves about ₹15,000 a year in tax.

documents: CEA shown as a separate component in your salary structure
Old regime choice in your employer's tax declaration
Children's details (names, ages, hostel status if applicable) if your employer asks
watchOut: Choose the old regime in your declaration, or your employer will not give you the exemption.
Only the first 2 children count.
Check that your salary structure actually has a CEA component. Employers often do not offer one.
Amounts above the limit are taxable.

lta.title: Leave Travel Allowance (LTA)
lta.short: Tax-free part of your salary for holiday travel within India.
lta.whatIsIt: LTA is a salary component your employer pays you to cover the fare of a holiday trip within India. If you actually travel and show proof, the part of LTA you spend on that fare is tax-free.
lta.benefit: You do not pay tax on the LTA you use for qualifying travel, so your taxable salary drops. There is no fixed rupee cap. The limit is how much LTA your employer pays you and what the trip actually cost. For someone in the 30% slab, every ₹1,00,000 of LTA that becomes exempt saves roughly ₹31,200 in tax (including 4% cess).
whoCanClaim: Salaried employees whose salary includes an LTA component.
You must be under the OLD tax regime. The exemption is not available in the new regime.
Travel can be for you, your spouse, your children, your parents, and brothers and sisters who depend mainly on you.
Children: only 2 count if they were born after 1 October 1998. There is no limit for children born before that, or for twins and other multiple births after that.

howCalculated.intro: The exempt amount is the LOWER of these two. Anything above it is taxable.
steps: The LTA your employer paid you.
The actual fare you spent on the trip, limited to the fare for the allowed mode of travel.

clauses.title: Old regime only
clauses.text: You can claim LTA exemption only if you choose the old tax regime.

clauses.title: Only the fare is covered
clauses.text: Hotels, food, sightseeing and local taxis are not covered. Only the travel fare counts.

clauses.title: Within India only
clauses.text: The trip must be inside India. A foreign trip does not qualify.

clauses.title: Fare limit by mode of travel
clauses.text: Air: economy class fare by the shortest route. Train: AC first class fare. Bus or other public transport: first class or deluxe fare. Own car or taxi: only the equivalent AC first class rail fare, even if you spent more.

clauses.title: 2 journeys in a block of 4 years
clauses.text: You can claim only 2 journeys in every block of 4 calendar years. Within a block you can claim in any year, in any order. The current block is 2026 to 2029. The previous block was 2022 to 2025.

clauses.title: One journey can be carried over
clauses.text: If you did not use both journeys in a block, you can carry over one journey into the first year of the next block, but not both.

clauses.title: Proof is needed
clauses.text: Keep tickets, boarding passes or travel bills. Your employer may ask for them.

clauses.title: Where it sits in the law
clauses.text: In the old Act this was Section 10(5) with Rule 2B. The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaced the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026. The exact new section number is not stated here until confirmed from the official text.

latestUpdate.headline: A new 4-year block started: 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2029.
details: The 2022 to 2025 block has ended. Two fresh journeys can be claimed in the 2026 to 2029 block.
Journeys made up to 31 December 2025 count in the old block. Journeys from 1 January 2026 count in the new block.
Proposed in draft rules, not confirmed as final: a new Form 124 replacing Form 12BB, mandatory proof of actual travel, and a cap of about ₹30 per kilometre on road travel.

example.scenario: Your LTA is ₹40,000 a year. You and your spouse fly to Goa, and the economy tickets cost ₹28,000 in total.

rows.label: A. LTA paid by your employer

example.result: Exempt LTA = lower of A and B = ₹28,000. The other ₹12,000 is taxable.
example.compare: At the 30% slab this saves about ₹8,700 in tax. This trip uses one of your 2 journeys in the 2026 to 2029 block, so one is left.

documents: Tickets, boarding passes or travel bills
Names of the family members who travelled
LTA claim form or declaration submitted to your employer
Old regime choice in your employer tax declaration
watchOut: Do not claim hotel, food or sightseeing bills. They are not covered.
Do not claim a foreign trip.
Track your journeys: only 2 in every block of 4 years.
Choose the old regime in your declaration, or your employer will not give you the exemption.
Keep proof of travel, not just a verbal claim.

car-fuel-driver.title: Car Fuel and Driver Benefit
car-fuel-driver.short: How much of your employer-paid car costs and driver is taxed.
car-fuel-driver.whatIsIt: Employers often pay for the fuel, upkeep and driver of a car you use. This is not a flat allowance. The tax law decides how much of that benefit is added to your taxable salary (called a perquisite). If the car is used only for official work and records are kept, nothing is added. If it is also used for personal trips, a fixed monthly amount is added.
car-fuel-driver.benefit: For a car used only for work, the employer pays the costs and none of it is taxed to you. For a car used partly for personal trips, you are taxed on a fixed monthly amount set by the rules, not on what your employer actually spends. In 2026 those fixed amounts went up, so this benefit now costs more tax than before.
whoCanClaim: Salaried employees whose employer provides a car, or reimburses fuel, maintenance or driver costs.
Official use only: the employer must keep a logbook and a certificate that the travel was for work.
The fixed-value method applies to cars used partly for official and partly for personal purposes.
Reported to apply the same way under the old and the new tax regime. Confirm this before relying on it.

howCalculated.intro: Work out which situation you are in, then add the fixed amount to your taxable salary for each month.
steps: Decide who owns the car and who pays the running costs (fuel and maintenance).
If the car is used only for official work with a logbook, the taxable amount is nil.
If it is used partly for personal trips, find your case in the table below and take the fixed monthly amount.
Add the driver amount on top if your employer also provides a driver. Multiply by the months you had the benefit.

table.heading: Fixed monthly taxable amount (from 1 April 2026)
rows: Employer-owned or hired car. Employer pays running costs.
Employer-owned or hired car. You pay the running costs of personal use.
Your own car. Employer reimburses running costs.

clauses.title: Official use only: nothing taxable
clauses.text: If the car is used only for work, the employer reimburses costs and keeps a logbook and a certificate, no perquisite arises.

clauses.title: Mixed use: fixed amount
clauses.text: If the car is also used for personal trips, a fixed monthly amount is added to your income, whatever the real cost.

clauses.title: Driver adds a second amount
clauses.text: If a driver is provided, the driver amount is added on top of the car amount.

clauses.title: Electric cars
clauses.text: Electric cars are grouped with cars up to 1.6 litres. The 2026 rules also clarified how electric cars are valued.

clauses.title: It is a taxable value, not a tax-free limit
clauses.text: These figures are amounts added to your taxable salary. They are not amounts you can receive tax-free.

clauses.title: Not the same as transport allowance
clauses.text: Ordinary transport allowance paid in your salary is a different thing and is mostly taxable.

clauses.title: Where it sits in the law
clauses.text: In the old Act this was Section 17(2) with Rule 3 of the 1962 Rules. The Income-tax Rules, 2026 came into force on 1 April 2026. The exact new rule number is not stated here until confirmed from the official text.

latestUpdate.headline: Taxable value of a car and driver benefit rose sharply.
details: Employer-paid car up to 1.6 litres: from ₹1,800 to ₹5,000 a month. Above 1.6 litres: from ₹2,400 to ₹7,000.
Driver: from ₹900 to ₹3,000 a month.
If you pay the personal-use running costs yourself: from ₹600 and ₹900 to ₹2,000 and ₹3,000.
Your own car with employer reimbursement uses the same amounts as an employer-paid car.
The change is a tax increase for employees who use a car for personal trips.

example.scenario: You have an employer-owned car with an engine above 1.6 litres. The employer pays running costs and provides a driver. You use it partly for personal trips.

rows.label: Added to your income a year, old
Added to your income a year, new

example.result: About ₹80,400 more taxable income a year.
example.compare: At the 30% slab that is roughly ₹25,000 more tax a year. If the same car were used only for official work with a logbook, nothing would be added.

documents: Logbook showing official and personal trips
Employer certificate that travel was for official work
Car details: who owns it and engine size
Employer records of fuel, maintenance and driver costs
watchOut: Without a logbook and employer certificate, official use may not be accepted.
Engine size decides which amount applies: up to 1.6 litres or above.
These are taxable amounts, not tax-free limits.
The amounts come from a secondary source and still need checking against the notified rules.
Later amendments to the Rules were notified in 2026. Check whether any of them changed these amounts.

nps.title: National Pension System (NPS)
nps.short: Tax deductions for retirement savings, including your employer's contribution.
nps.calcHeading: How the deduction is worked out
nps.whatIsIt: NPS is a government-regulated retirement savings scheme. Money goes in during your working years and is invested. At retirement you take part of it as a lump sum and use the rest to buy a pension. On this page we only cover the tax side, which has three parts: your own contribution, an extra ₹50,000, and your employer's contribution.
nps.benefit: What goes into NPS is cut from your taxable income, up to a limit, so you pay less tax. The employer contribution is the most useful part: it works in both tax regimes and sits outside the ₹1,50,000 Section 80C limit. For someone in the 30% slab, every ₹1,00,000 that becomes deductible saves roughly ₹31,200 in tax (including 4% cess).
whoCanClaim: Salaried employees who have an NPS account.
Employer contribution: available in both the old and the new tax regime. Your employer must pay it into your NPS account, usually set up through payroll.
Your own contribution and the extra ₹50,000: old tax regime only.

howCalculated.intro: There are three separate deductions. Work out each one, then add them up.
steps: Employer contribution: the amount your employer pays into your NPS, up to 14% of your Basic + DA in the new regime. It is on top of the ₹1,50,000 Section 80C limit.
Your own contribution (old regime): counts inside the ₹1,50,000 Section 80C limit, and up to 10% of your Basic + DA.
Extra ₹50,000 (old regime): an additional deduction for your own contribution, on top of the ₹1,50,000.

table.heading: The three NPS tax benefits
rows: Inside the ₹1,50,000 Section 80C limit; up to 10% of Basic + DA
Up to 14% of Basic + DA in the new regime

clauses.title: Employer contribution survives in the new regime
clauses.text: It is the only NPS deduction that remains in the new regime. Your own contribution and the extra ₹50,000 are not available there.

clauses.title: Limit is a share of Basic + DA
clauses.text: The limit is a percentage of your Basic + DA, not of your total pay. A small basic means a small limit.

clauses.title: Extra room beyond Section 80C
clauses.text: The employer contribution does not use up your ₹1,50,000 Section 80C limit.

clauses.title: Above the limit is taxable
clauses.text: Employer contributions above the limit are taxed as salary.

clauses.title: Combined ₹7,50,000 cap
clauses.text: Your employer's yearly contributions to NPS, EPF and superannuation together are taxed once they pass ₹7,50,000.

clauses.title: Needs payroll set-up
clauses.text: Ask your employer to route part of your pay as an employer NPS contribution. You cannot claim it later on your own.

clauses.title: Old-regime cap for private employers
clauses.text: Sources disagree on whether it is 10% or 14% of Basic + DA. This is not stated here until confirmed.

clauses.title: Where it sits in the law
clauses.text: Old Section 80CCD. The Income-tax Act, 2025 reportedly moved it to Section 124, but sources disagree on the exact mapping, so the new numbers are not stated here. Form 16 and payslips may still show the old 80CCD label.

latestUpdate.headline: No change in the 14% limit found. NPS deductions move to a new section number.
details: The 14% employer limit in the new regime continues for 2026-27.
The Income-tax Act, 2025 reportedly moves these deductions to Section 124. Sources disagree on the exact mapping.
The old-regime limit for private employers is reported inconsistently (10% or 14%).
The extra ₹50,000 and your own contribution are still old-regime only.

example.scenario: Your Basic + DA is ₹60,000 a month, which is ₹7,20,000 a year. You are in the 30% slab.

rows.label: Extra ₹50,000 of your own, old regime only (₹50,000 × 31.2%)

example.result: Employer contribution alone saves about ₹31,450 a year, in either regime.
example.compare: In the old regime you can add the ₹50,000 deduction for about ₹15,600 more. Both are on top of your ₹1,50,000 Section 80C limit.

documents: Your PRAN (NPS account number)
Employer confirmation of the contribution made
NPS statement of contributions for the year
Old or new regime choice in your employer tax declaration
watchOut: Only the employer contribution works in the new regime.
The limit is based on Basic + DA, so check your salary structure.
Contributions above the limit are taxable.
Employer NPS, EPF and superannuation together are taxed above ₹7,50,000 a year.
Money in NPS is locked in until retirement. Check the withdrawal rules before putting money in.

gifts.title: Gift Vouchers and Gifts
gifts.short: Tax-free gifts and vouchers from your employer, up to a yearly limit.
gifts.calcHeading: How the tax is worked out
gifts.whatIsIt: Your employer can give you gifts, vouchers or tokens during the year, such as a Diwali hamper or a shopping voucher. If their total value stays within a limit, there is no tax on them. If it goes over, the whole amount becomes taxable.
gifts.benefit: A gift gives you value without it being added to your salary. A ₹10,000 voucher costs the employer ₹10,000 and you pay no tax on it. The same ₹10,000 paid as a bonus would be taxed at your slab rate, which is ₹3,120 at the 30% slab (including 4% cess).
whoCanClaim: Any employee who receives gifts, vouchers or tokens from the employer.
Reported to work under both the old and the new tax regime. Confirm this before relying on it.
Only real gifts, or vouchers and tokens that cannot be turned into cash, qualify.

howCalculated.intro: Add up every gift and voucher you got from your employer in the year, then compare with the limit.
steps: Leave out anything in cash, or that can be turned into cash. That is fully taxable.
Add the value of all other gifts, vouchers and tokens received in the year.
If the total is within the limit (₹15,000 from 1 April 2026), none of it is taxed.
If the total is above the limit, the whole amount is taxable, not just the excess.

table.heading: What is taxed and what is not
rows: Voucher you can redeem for cash
Gift, or voucher you cannot turn into cash. Yearly total within the limit.
Same gifts, yearly total above the limit

clauses.title: Cash never counts
clauses.text: A gift in cash, or one that can be turned into cash, such as a gift cheque, is fully taxable.

clauses.title: The limit is per year, in total
clauses.text: All gifts and vouchers received across the year are added together and compared with one limit.

clauses.title: It is a cliff, not a slope
clauses.text: If the total goes over the limit, the whole amount is taxable, not just the part above the limit.

clauses.title: A gift allowance is not a gift
clauses.text: A cash gift allowance shown on your payslip is taxable. Only an actual gift or voucher qualifies.

clauses.title: Not the ₹50,000 gift limit
clauses.text: The ₹50,000 figure in some headlines is for gifts you receive from friends and other non-relatives. It does not apply to employer gifts.

clauses.title: Meal vouchers are separate
clauses.text: Meal vouchers are reported as exempt up to ₹200 per meal from 1 April 2026. That is its own component.

clauses.title: Exactly ₹15,000
clauses.text: One source says no tax applies only when the value is below ₹15,000. Another says up to and including ₹15,000. This is not settled here, so stay below ₹15,000.

clauses.title: Where it sits in the law
clauses.text: In the old Act this was Rule 3(7)(iv) of the 1962 Rules, under the perquisite rules for salary. The Income-tax Rules, 2026 came into force on 1 April 2026. The exact new rule number is not stated here until confirmed from the official text.

latestUpdate.headline: Tax-free limit for gifts and vouchers raised from ₹5,000 to ₹15,000 a year.
details: The old limit was ₹5,000 a year in total.
The new limit is ₹15,000 a year in total, from 1 April 2026.
Reported to apply under both the old and the new tax regime.
Whether exactly ₹15,000 is tax-free is disputed in the sources. Stay below it.

example.scenario: Your employer gives you a ₹10,000 Diwali voucher and a ₹4,000 birthday hamper, ₹14,000 in total.

rows.label: If the total were ₹16,000: taxable amount

example.result: Under the new limit nothing is taxable. Under the old limit it would have cost about ₹4,370 at the 30% slab.
example.compare: At ₹16,000 the whole amount is taxable because of the cliff. Staying below the limit matters.

documents: Employer record of gifts and vouchers given during the year
Voucher terms showing it cannot be redeemed for cash
Your own total for the year, across all occasions
watchOut: Cash and gift cheques are always taxable.
A voucher you can redeem for cash is taxable.
Going over the limit makes the whole amount taxable.
Add up all occasions in the year, not each gift on its own.
Do not plan right at ₹15,000. Stay below it.
The limit comes from secondary sources and still needs checking against the notified rules.
